org.lleverage.pptPalette.$note: The PPT drawing palette: the names work/drawing-pages.js uses for its colours, bound to the tokens they are. Until 22 Sep these were seventeen hand-typed hex literals on line 2 of that file -- the largest remaining second source in the repo, and exactly what emit-css.js fails the build for on the CSS side. Sixteen matched a token exactly. This map is the ONE place the binding is stated: work/build-templates.js resolves it into ppt/theme.json and verifyTheme re-resolves it from here, so neither restates the other. The names say what they are since 23 Sep: CARD was renamed SANDACC (sand.accent, an emphasis fill for a column or a caption band, NEVER a card, which is WHITE since 8 Sep) and SAGE4 SAGE2 (it was always sage.200). KICK was bound to sage.900 until 23 Sep, so every kicker and label in the master was Sage 900, which text.kicker says is not label text; it is Grey 700 now. G9 is grey.900: the icon ghost, typed as 232724 with no token until the owner adopted Grey 900 (7 apart) on 23 Sep, which removed the last exception to the raw-hex guard.

deck.$description: Line spacing, as a percentage of the type size, one per role in the deck ramp. Percentages rather than points so one number serves every venue and each emitter resolves it: work/layouts.js writes <a:spcPts> in points, kit/system.js writes points for pptxgenjs. These are the values work/layouts.js has carried as literals since step 4; they are not new numbers, they are the same numbers with a source. Leading had no token until 22 Sep, which is how <a:spcPct> shipped for eleven days meaning a percentage of the FONT line box (118% of the em for the text faces, 132% for the mono) rather than of the size — a hairline through WHAT IT MEASURES on three pages, and the single most expensive bug on the presentations skill's own build.

canvas.$description: The canvas every number in grid is a fraction of, and the factor for turning those units into inches or points. Its own group rather than part of grid because it is not a CSS length: work/emit-css.js writes every grid key out as px, and an inch value stamped px is nonsense. It had no token at all until 22 Sep, and that omission is the whole of the 23 vs 32 pt confusion. A point is an absolute 1/72 inch, so without the canvas a point size cannot be carried between two decks and stay the same size. The master is 13.333 x 7.5 in, PowerPoint Widescreen; pptxgenjs's LAYOUT_16x9 default is 10 x 5.625 in, the same shape 1.3333x smaller. 23 pt on that canvas is 30.67 pt on this one, 4% off the 32 pt here -- the same design, read as a disagreement because nobody wrote the canvas down. Normalised, margin, content width and content top agree to a tenth of a percent. Anything emitting inches or points MUST derive them through unitsPerInch and never restate them.

$extensions.note: PowerPoint Widescreen 16:9, and what master/*.pptx declares in sldSz

grid.slideUnits / grid.slideWidth. The one factor every inch conversion goes through — never restate an inch value, derive it

table.$description: A table is marked by its head and its total, nothing else: no fill on the head, no vertical or outer rules, no bands by default, no highlight column (decided 10 Sep). The head is bold Public Sans at the venue's body size, not mono (the owner, 23 Sep). The stylesheet, the PowerPoint table style and the skills read this; until 23 Sep it was typed into emit-css.js, the template's default table style was Office's orange-headed banded one, and the component page described zebra rows in a grey the CSS did not draw.

size.$description: a type role, resolved per venue: type.deck.body in a deck, type.doc.body in a document

fill.$description: table.zebra only: a long table where the eye has to track a row. Its rows lose their rules.

process.$description: A row of steps joined by emphasis arrows. The active step takes the orange outline; a step a person performs takes the orange hatch, its label set bold straight on the hatch. Balance first: the steps in a row are one height, the tallest label's, and a short label centres in its box rather than shrinking it. Unequal heights are allowed when they carry meaning (a step drawn to its duration, say) and are then chosen, never the accident of one label wrapping to two lines (the owner, 5 Oct).

heights.$description: equal: every step in a row takes the tallest step's height, label centred. natural: each step to its own content, opted into per diagram (.process.natural), only when the difference means something.

$extensions.decided: 5 Oct 2026 -- the owner: 'Balance should be key. Those boxes should be same height', with room to choose otherwise. Until then .process centred steps of their content height, so a two-line label stood taller than its neighbours.

hatch.$description: the human step's hatch lines and outline

ground.$description: what shows between the hatch lines: the page ground, the same as every other step. Never white, and no plate under the label.

$extensions.decided: 5 Oct 2026 -- the owner: the white plate the master set under the hatched step's label 'does not work'; a plate in the page ground was not wanted either. The label sits on the hatch itself, in bold (label.weight).
